## Problem

System has 1,649 Python scripts + 9 SQLite DBs but all intelligence runs on LLM at runtime. ~70% of local intelligence infrastructure is phantom (code exists, zero data). LLM causes hallucination. System must continuously demand quality data from LLM to evolve locally.

## Approved Design

### Architecture: Continuous Knowledge Hunger Engine

**Runtime:** Claude Code session (hooks)
**Provider:** Current Claude session (no separate API)
**Priority:** User-driven (most-queried domains first)
**Budget:** Unlimited per cycle, stop when satiated
**Storage:** SQLite decision_vectors.db in master_investments
**Triggers:** SessionStart + Post-verdict + On-demand (/feed)

### Two Parallel Threads

**Thread 1: Hunger Loop (active learning)**
- Gap detector scans all domains, ranks by user query frequency
- Question generator creates surgical LLM research requests (structured JSON)
- LLM researches → verifier cross-checks → store in SQLite
- Loop until satiated (coverage ≥90%, confidence ≥0.8, no new facts 3 cycles)

**Thread 2: Distillation Engine (batch extraction)**
- Extract decisions from existing sources (PATP files, case studies, evidence JSONs)
- No LLM needed for structured data, LLM only for book text extraction
- Runs during idle moments in session

### Stop Conditions (Satiation)
- Domain coverage ≥ 90%
- No new unique facts in last 3 consecutive cycles
- All contradictions resolved
- Average confidence ≥ 0.8
- No fact older than 180 days without recheck

### Domain Ranking Formula
```
hunger_score = query_frequency × (1 - coverage) × staleness_factor
```

### SQLite Schema
- `decision_vectors`: domain, dimension, fact, value, mechanism, confidence, source, corroboration count
- `domain_coverage`: per-domain metrics (query_count, dimensions filled/total, avg_confidence)
- `hunger_log`: cycle audit trail (facts added/updated, coverage delta, stop reason)

### 8 Knowledge Dimensions Per Domain
1. failure_rates (base rate)
2. unit_economics (margins, CAC, LTV)
3. competitive_landscape (top 10 players)
4. moat_patterns (what works/doesn't)
5. founder_paths (real examples with revenue)
6. timing_windows (market cycle position)
7. regulatory_risks (platform, legal, tax)
8. compounding_mechanisms (data, network, IP, distribution)

### Hook Integration
- **SessionStart**: Scan top 3 domains, feed if coverage <70%, refresh stale facts
- **Post-verdict**: Extract ALL agent claims (free intelligence), store, queue new gaps
- **On-demand**: /feed command for manual trigger

### Anti-Hallucination
- LLM returns structured JSON only, no prose
- Every claim must have source_url + source_date
- Local KB provides FLOOR — LLM can add but can't contradict verified facts
- Magnitude checks (claim exceeds 3σ from KB mean → FLAG)
- Staleness checks (fact >180 days → tentative until re-verified)

## Dependencies
- Knowledge Distillation Engine plan (plans/260510-0914-knowledge-distillation-engine/)
- LFI Architecture plan (plans/260510-0952-local-first-intelligence-architecture/)
- This engine is Phase 0.5 — bridges between distillation (seed data) and full LFI (local verdict)

## Success Metrics
- Month 1: 500+ decision vectors, LLM dependency 80%→60%
- Month 3: 2000+ vectors, local pre-screen handles 30% of queries
- Month 6: 5000+ vectors, local verdict for 60%+ queries, LLM <10%

## Target Repo
master_investments (NOT _mmo)

Base directory for this skill: D:\code\invesments\master_investments_mmo\.claude\skills\ck-plan

# Planning

Create detailed technical implementation plans through research, codebase analysis, solution design, and comprehensive documentation.

## Prerequisites

- **ClaudeKit CLI required:** This skill requires `ck` CLI for plan operations.
  Run `npm install -g claudekit` if not installed.

## CLI Integration

This skill orchestrates planning, but ClaudeKit CLI now owns the plan file scaffolding and phase state mutations whenever `ck` is available.

Use these commands instead of hand-editing CLI-managed plan structure:

```bash
ck plan create \
  --title "{plan title}" \
  --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \
  --dir {plan-dir} \
  --source skill

ck plan create \
  --global \
  --title "{plan title}" \
  --phases "{Research},{Implement},{Test}" \
  --dir {plan-dir} \
  --source skill

cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check <phase-id> --start
cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan check <phase-id>
cd /absolute/path/to/plan-dir && ck plan uncheck <phase-id>
ck plan status /absolute/path/to/plan.md
ck config ui --port 3456
```

Rules:
- Use `ck plan create` to scaffold `plan.md` and `phase-*.md` when the CLI is available.
- Default scope is project-local (`./plans/` under the current project).
- Global scope is conditional: use `ck plan create --global ...` or fall back to global scope only when no project context exists.
- Use `ck plan check` / `ck plan uncheck` for phase status changes.
- Do not hand-edit the phases table for status toggles or structural updates when CLI commands are available.
- Use the dashboard at `http://localhost:3456/plans` for visual plan management.
- **Overwriting phase stub files:** `ck plan create` scaffolds small boilerplate `phase-XX-*.md` stubs. Always **Read the stub before Write** — Claude Code enforces Read-before-Write on existing files; skipping the Read causes the Write to be rejected, wasting the Write's input tokens AND forcing a retry. The stubs are tiny (~15 lines), so the Read cost is trivial. Then Write the full content following the canonical template below.

### Canonical Phase File Template

Use this structure when filling each `phase-XX-*.md`. Loaded once with the skill — no per-file Read needed to learn it. Frontmatter fields match the CLI's phase schema; section headers match `documentation-management.md` so phase files stay consistent across plans.

````markdown
---
phase: <N>
title: "<Phase Name>"
status: pending       # pending | in-progress | completed
priority: P2          # P1 | P2 | P3
effort: ""            # e.g. "4h", "2d"
dependencies: []      # phase IDs this blocks on
---

# Phase <id>: <Name>

## Overview
<1-2 sentences describing what this phase delivers>

## Requirements
- Functional: ...
- Non-functional: ...

## Architecture
<Design, data flow, component interactions>

## Related Code Files
- Create: `path/...`
- Modify: `path/...`
- Delete: `path/...`

## Implementation Steps
1. ...
2. ...

## Success Criteria
- [ ] ...

## Risk Assessment
<Risks + mitigations>
````

**IMPORTANT:** Before you start, scan unfinished plans in the active scope first:
- Project scope: `./plans/`
- Global scope: the configured global plans root
  - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/`

If there are relevant plans overlapping your upcoming plan, update them as well. If you're unsure or need more clarifications, use `AskUserQuestion` tool to ask the user.

### Scope Selection

- **Project scope** is the default whenever the current working tree has project context.
- **Global scope** is allowed only when:
  - the user explicitly asks for it via `--global`, or
  - there is no project context to anchor a local plan.
- **No project context** means no `.git`, `package.json`, or `CLAUDE.md` was found in the ancestor chain.
- Keep scope honest in prose and examples: the skill describes CLI-owned behavior, it does not implement scope resolution itself.

### Cross-Plan Dependency Detection

During the pre-creation scan, detect and mark blocking relationships between plans:

1. **Scan** — Read `plan.md` frontmatter of each unfinished plan (status != `completed`/`cancelled`)
2. **Compare scope** — Check overlapping files, shared dependencies, same feature area
3. **Classify relationship:**
   - New plan needs output of existing plan → new plan `blockedBy: [existing-plan-dir]`
   - New plan changes something existing plan depends on → existing plan `blockedBy: [new-plan-dir]`, new plan `blocks: [existing-plan-dir]`
   - Cross-scope dependency → use `global:` or `project:` prefixes
   - Mutual dependency → both plans reference each other in `blockedBy`/`blocks`
4. **Bidirectional update** — When relationship detected, update BOTH `plan.md` files' frontmatter
5. **Ambiguous?** → Use `AskUserQuestion` with header "Plan Dependency", present detected overlap, ask user to confirm relationship type (blocks/blockedBy/none)

**Frontmatter fields**:
```yaml
blockedBy: [260301-1200-auth-system]            # Same-scope dependency
blockedBy: [global:260301-1200-auth-system]     # Cross-scope dependency
blocks: [project:260228-0900-user-dashboard]    # Explicit project-scope dependency
```

**Status interaction:** `ck plan status` is the authoritative inspection surface. Same-scope bare refs stay in the current scope; prefixed refs resolve against the explicit project/global root. Missing refs should warn and show `not found`, not hard-fail the plan.

## Default (No Arguments)

If invoked with a task description, proceed with planning workflow. If invoked WITHOUT arguments or with unclear intent, use `AskUserQuestion` to present available operations:

| Operation | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `(default)` | Create implementation plan for a task |
| `archive` | Write journal entry & archive plans |
| `red-team` | Adversarial plan review |
| `validate` | Critical questions interview |

Present as options via `AskUserQuestion` with header "Planning Operation", question "What would you like to do?".

## Workflow Modes

Default: `--auto` (analyze task complexity and auto-pick mode).

| Flag | Mode | Research | Red Team | Validation | Cook Flag |
|------|------|----------|----------|------------|-----------|
| `--auto` | Auto-detect | Follows mode | Follows mode | Follows mode | Follows mode |
| `--fast` | Fast | Skip | Skip | Skip | `--auto` |
| `--hard` | Hard | 2 researchers | Yes | Optional | (none) |
| `--deep` | Deep | 2-3 researchers + per-phase scout | Yes | Yes | (none) |
| `--parallel` | Parallel | 2 researchers | Yes | Optional | `--parallel` |
| `--two` | Two approaches | 2+ researchers | After selection | After selection | (none) |

**Composable flags** (combine with any mode):
| Flag | Effect |
|------|--------|
| `--tdd` | Add tests-first structure to each phase for regression-safe refactors |
| `--no-tasks` | Skip task hydration |

Load: `references/workflow-modes.md` for auto-detection logic, per-mode workflows, context reminders.

## When to Use

- Planning new feature implementations
- Architecting system designs
- Evaluating technical approaches
- Creating implementation roadmaps
- Breaking down complex requirements

## Core Responsibilities & Rules

Always honoring **YAGNI**, **KISS**, and **DRY** principles.
**Be honest, be brutal, straight to the point, and be concise.**

### 0. Scope Challenge
Load: `references/scope-challenge.md`
**Skip if:** `--fast` mode or trivial task (single file fix, <20 word description)

### 1. Research & Analysis
Load: `references/research-phase.md`
**Skip if:** Fast mode or provided with researcher reports

### 2. Codebase Understanding
Load: `references/codebase-understanding.md`
**Skip if:** Provided with scout reports

### 3. Solution Design
Load: `references/solution-design.md`

### 4. Plan Creation & Organization
Load: `references/plan-organization.md`

### 5. Task Breakdown & Output Standards
Load: `references/output-standards.md`

## Process Flow (Authoritative)

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A[Pre-Creation Check] --> B[Cross-Plan Scan]
    B --> C[Scope Challenge]
    C --> D[Mode Detection]
    D -->|fast| E[Skip Research]
    D -->|hard/deep/parallel/two| F[Spawn Researchers]
    E --> G[Codebase Analysis]
    F --> G
    G --> H[Write Plan via Planner]
    H --> I{Red Team?}
    I -->|Yes| J[Red Team Review]
    I -->|No| K{Validate?}
    J --> K
    K -->|Yes| V[Verification Pass]
    K -->|No| M[Hydrate Tasks]
    V --> L[Validation Interview]
    L --> M
    M --> N[Output Cook Command]
    N --> O[Journal]
```

**This diagram is the authoritative workflow.** Prose sections below provide detail for each node.

## Workflow Process

1. **Pre-Creation Check** → Check Plan Context for active/suggested/none
1b. **Cross-Plan Scan** → Scan unfinished plans, detect `blockedBy`/`blocks` relationships, update both plans
1c. **Scope Challenge** → Run Step 0 scope questions, select mode (see `references/scope-challenge.md`)
    **Skip if:** `--fast` mode or trivial task
2. **Mode Detection** → Auto-detect or use explicit flag (see `workflow-modes.md`)
3. **Research Phase** → Spawn researchers (skip in fast mode)
4. **Codebase Analysis** → Read docs, scout if needed
5. **Plan Documentation** → Write comprehensive plan via planner subagent
6. **Red Team Review** → Run `/ck:plan red-team {plan-path}` (hard/deep/parallel/two modes)
7. **Post-Plan Validation** → Run `/ck:plan validate {plan-path}` (hard/deep/parallel/two modes)
8. **Hydrate Tasks** → Create Claude Tasks from phases (default on, `--no-tasks` to skip)
9. **Context Reminder** → Output cook command with absolute path (MANDATORY)
10. **Journal** → Run `/ck:journal` to write a concise technical journal entry upon completion

## Output Requirements
**IMPORTANT:** Invoke "/ck:project-organization" skill to organize the outputs.

- DO NOT implement code - only create plans
- Respond with plan file path and summary
- Ensure self-contained plans with necessary context
- Include code snippets/pseudocode when clarifying
- Fully respect the `./docs/development-rules.md` file

## Task Management

Plan files = persistent. Tasks = session-scoped. Hydration bridges the gap.

**Default:** Auto-hydrate tasks after plan files are written. Skip with `--no-tasks`.
**3-Task Rule:** <3 phases → skip task creation.
**Fallback:** Task tools (`TaskCreate`/`TaskUpdate`/`TaskGet`/`TaskList`) are CLI-only — unavailable in VSCode extension. If they error, use `TodoWrite` for tracking. Plan files remain the source of truth; hydration is an optimization, not a requirement.

Load: `references/task-management.md` for hydration pattern, TaskCreate patterns, cook handoff protocol.

### Hydration Workflow
1. Write plan.md + phase files (persistent layer)
2. TaskCreate per phase with `addBlockedBy` chain (skip if Task tools unavailable)
3. TaskCreate for critical/high-risk steps within phases (skip if Task tools unavailable)
4. Metadata: phase, priority, effort, planDir, phaseFile
5. Cook picks up via TaskList (same session) or re-hydrates (new session)

## Active Plan State

Check `## Plan Context` injected by hooks:
- **"Plan: {path}"** → Active plan. Ask "Continue? [Y/n]"
- **"Suggested: {path}"** → Branch hint only. Ask if activate or create new.
- **"Plan: none"** → Create new using `Plan dir:` from `## Naming`

After creating plan: `node .claude/scripts/set-active-plan.cjs {plan-dir}`
Reports: Active plans → plan-specific path. Suggested → default path.

### Important
**DO NOT** create plans or reports in arbitrary user directories.
**MUST** create plans or reports in one of these allowed roots:
- project scope → current working project directory
- global scope → configured global plans root
  - Default when unset: `~/.claude/plans/`

## Subcommands

| Subcommand | Reference | Purpose |
|------------|-----------|---------|
| `/ck:plan archive` | `references/archive-workflow.md` | Archive plans + write journal entries |
| `/ck:plan red-team` | `references/red-team-workflow.md` | Adversarial plan review with hostile reviewers |
| `/ck:plan validate` | `references/validate-workflow.md` | Validate plan with critical questions interview |

## Quality Standards

- Thorough and specific, consider long-term maintainability
- Research thoroughly when uncertain
- Address security and performance concerns
- Detailed enough for junior developers
- Validate against existing codebase patterns

**Remember:** Plan quality determines implementation success. Be comprehensive and consider all solution aspects.

## Workflow Position

**Typically follows:** `/ck:brainstorm` (after exploring options), `/ck:scout` (after codebase discovery)
**Typically precedes:** `/ck:cook` (hand off plan for implementation)
**Related:** `/ck:brainstorm` (explore before planning), `/ck:cook` (execute after planning)

# Knowledge Distillation Engine — Plan Overview

## Problem

Stage0/master_investments has 1,649 Python scripts + 9 SQLite DBs + 162 persona decisions — but intelligence runs 100% on LLM at runtime. Local infra exists but sits empty (compound.db = 0 rows, confidence-caps = empty, outcomes = 0). System can't evolve because feedback loop requires personal action outcomes that don't exist yet.

## Solution

Use LLM as offline knowledge extraction engine: mine real decisions from books, case studies, and failure post-mortems. Convert to structured feature vectors. Build local reasoning engine that matches new opportunities against 500+ distilled decisions WITHOUT calling LLM. LLM becomes fallback for novel cases only.

## Architecture

```
LLM (offline, 1-time runs)
  |
  | distill: books, case studies, failures
  v
Local Knowledge DB (SQLite, permanent)
  - decision_vectors (500+ structured decisions)
  - kill_signals (100+ death patterns)
  - success_signals (100+ positive indicators)
  - pattern_rules (50+ if-then rules)
  |
  v
Local Reasoning Engine (Python, instant)
  - pattern_match() → top-K similar decisions
  - kill_scan() → immediate red flags
  - score() → CENTS/ESBI/leverage scores
  - verdict() → KILL/PASS/NEEDS_LLM
  |
  | only if confidence < 60%
  v
LLM (runtime fallback for novel cases)
```

## Phases

| # | Phase | Effort | Status |
|---|-------|--------|--------|
| P1 | [Vectorize 162 existing decisions](phase-01-vectorize-existing-decisions.md) | 1 day | ✅ complete (205 vectors) |
| P2 | [Build local reasoning engine](phase-02-local-reasoning-engine.md) | 2 days | ✅ complete (295 LOC, 77% accuracy) |
| P3 | [Distillation run: Top 3 books](phase-03-distill-books.md) | 1 day | ⏸ deferred (books not yet sourced) |
| P4 | [Distillation run: Failures + Indie Hackers](phase-04-distill-failures.md) | 1 day | ⏸ deferred |
| P5 | [Wire into stage0 pipeline](phase-05-wire-stage0.md) | 1 day | ✅ complete (stage0.md wired) |
| P6 | [Auto-distillation hook](phase-06-auto-distillation.md) | 0.5 day | ✅ complete (auto-distill-case.py) |

# Local-First Intelligence Architecture (LFI)

## Problem

master_investments intelligence runs ~40% on LLM at runtime. This causes:
1. **Hallucination** — LLM fabricates metrics, expresses false confidence, gives inconsistent verdicts
2. **Vendor lock-in** — 6 files call `anthropic` SDK directly, bypassing provider interface
3. **No evolution** — System doesn't learn from LLM interactions; each session starts fresh
4. **Cost & latency** — LLM calls = $0.003-0.015/call + 5-30s vs <200ms local

## Solution

4-tier architecture where LLM is demoted to "research tool + fallback":

```
T4: AUTONOMY GOVERNOR — graduated auto/semi/human per domain accuracy
T3: LOCAL REASONING    — decision vectors + chains + rules → VERDICT (<200ms)
T2: KNOWLEDGE DISTILLER — LLM output → extract → verify → store locally
T1: LLM INTERFACE      — structured extraction + anti-hallucination + provider-agnostic
```

## Architecture Principles

1. **LLM never outputs verdicts** — only structured, verifiable facts
2. **Every LLM fact gets provenance** — source_llm, query, date, verified_by
3. **Cross-query validation** — same fact queried 2x with different wording
4. **Coverage tracking** — system knows what it knows and what it doesn't
5. **Graduated autonomy** — domain accuracy < 85% = human confirm

## Phases

| # | Phase | Effort | Status | Deps |
|---|-------|--------|--------|------|
| P1 | [LLM Provider Abstraction + Anti-Hallucination](./phase-01-llm-provider-abstraction-anti-hallucination.md) | 3-4d | ✅ complete | KDE P1-P2 |
| P2 | [Coverage Tracker + Gap Detector](./phase-02-coverage-tracker-gap-detector.md) | 2-3d | ✅ complete | P1 |
| P3 | [Reasoning Chain Engine](./phase-03-reasoning-chain-engine.md) | 4-5d | ✅ complete | KDE complete |
| P4 | [Evolution Triggers](./phase-04-evolution-triggers-session-outcome-continuous.md) | 3-4d | ✅ complete | P1+P2 |
| P5 | [Autonomy Governor](./phase-05-autonomy-governor.md) | 2-3d | ✅ complete | P3 |
| P6 | [Integration Test + Calibration](./phase-06-integration-test-calibration.md) | 2-3d | ✅ complete | P1-P5 |

KDE = Knowledge Distillation Engine (prerequisite plan: `260510-0914-knowledge-distillation-engine/`)

## Dependencies

- **blockedBy:** `260510-0914-knowledge-distillation-engine` — P1-P2 of KDE must complete first (need vectors + local engine)
- P1 can start in parallel with KDE P3-P6
- P3 requires KDE complete (needs distilled rules to chain)
- P4 requires P1+P2 (needs provider abstraction + gap detection)
- P5 requires P3 (needs local verdicts to govern)
- P6 requires all phases

## Success Criteria

- [x] LLM dependency ratio: ~40% → <10%
- [x] Zero direct `anthropic` SDK calls outside provider adapter
- [x] Every LLM fact has provenance tag in local DB
- [x] Hallucination rate measurable and tracked (target: <5% of verified facts)
- [x] 3 evolution triggers active (session, outcome, continuous)
- [x] Domain-level accuracy tracking with auto-graduation
- [x] Local verdict latency <200ms for 90%+ of cases
- [x] Token cost per case drops 5x for matched cases

## Kill Criteria

- Local engine accuracy < 70% on 50+ verdicts → redesign feature schema
- Anti-hallucination overhead > 3x cost of raw LLM → simplify verification
- Evolution triggers produce < 5 new vectors/week → triggers not detecting gaps

# Knowledge Hunger Engine

## Problem

LFI infrastructure is deployed (81 tests passing) but the system is PASSIVE — only learns when user runs /stage0. Wave 1/2 agents return prose, not structured data. Post-verdict distillation doesn't extract claims. Gap detector exists but nothing feeds it research results. The evolution loop has no fuel.

## Solution

Build the missing fuel pipeline: agents output structured JSON → post-verdict extracts claims → hunger loop detects gaps → generates targeted questions → fires LLM research → verifies → stores → repeats until satiated. System actively DEMANDS knowledge instead of waiting.

## Existing Infrastructure (in master_investments)

| Component | Location | Status |
|-----------|----------|--------|
| Coverage tracker + gap detector | .claude/lib/intelligence/coverage/ | ✅ Deployed, 16 tests |
| Reasoning chain engine | .claude/lib/intelligence/reasoning/ | ✅ Deployed, 28 tests |

| Autonomy governor | .claude/lib/intelligence/governance/ | ✅ Deployed, 8 tests |
| decision-vectors.db | .claude/data/knowledge-distillation/ | ✅ 205 vectors |
| SessionStart hook | .claude/hooks/evolution-auto-runner.cjs | ✅ Wired |

## What This Plan Adds

1. **Structured agent output schema** — JSON format for all 14 Wave agents (fuel line)
2. **Hunger loop orchestrator** — Gap→question→research→verify→store cycle
3. **Post-verdict auto-distill** — Extract claims from every /stage0 run (free intelligence)
4. **Feed command + hook wiring** — /feed trigger + SessionStart hunger cycle
5. **Satiation calibration** — Stop conditions, domain priority, convergence testing

## Phases

| # | Phase | Effort | Status | Deps |
|---|-------|--------|--------|------|
| P1 | [Structured Agent Output Schema](./phase-01-structured-agent-output-schema.md) | 2d | Pending | None |
| P2 | [Hunger Loop Orchestrator](./phase-02-hunger-loop-orchestrator.md) | 2-3d | Pending | P1 |
| P3 | [Post-Verdict Auto-Distill](./phase-03-post-verdict-auto-distill.md) | 1-2d | Pending | P1 |
| P4 | [Feed Command and Hook Wiring](./phase-04-feed-command-and-hook-wiring.md) | 1d | Pending | P2+P3 |
| P5 | [Satiation Calibration and Testing](./phase-05-satiation-calibration-and-testing.md) | 1-2d | Pending | P2+P4 |

- P2 and P3 can run in parallel after P1
- P4 requires both P2 and P3
- P5 is final integration + calibration

## Dependencies

- **Builds on:** LFI Architecture (260510-0952, COMPLETE)
- **Builds on:** Knowledge Distillation Engine (260510-0914, COMPLETE — P3/P4 deferred)
- **No blockers** — all prerequisites shipped

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 14 Wave agents output structured JSON with claims array
- [ ] Hunger loop processes ≥50 facts per cycle from gap-driven research
- [ ] Post-verdict auto-distill extracts ≥5 claims per /stage0 run
- [ ] /feed command triggers manual hunger cycle
- [ ] SessionStart hook runs hunger cycle automatically
- [ ] Satiation detector stops when coverage ≥90% AND no new facts 3 cycles
- [ ] decision-vectors.db grows from 205 → 500+ within 10 /stage0 runs
- [ ] Domain coverage tracked per user query frequency

## Kill Criteria

- Hunger loop produces <2 new verified facts per LLM call → question quality too low
- Post-distill claims accuracy <60% when spot-checked → extraction schema broken
- Satiation never triggers (infinite loop) → stop conditions miscalibrated

# Phase 2: Hunger Loop Orchestrator

## Overview

The core loop: detect gaps → generate questions → fire LLM research → verify answers → store in KB → check satiation → repeat. Integrates with existing gap_detector.py and distillation_bridge.py from LFI.

## Requirements

- Functional: Autonomous loop that fills knowledge gaps using LLM as research tool
- Functional: User-driven domain priority (most-queried domains fed first)
- Functional: Satiation detection (stop when coverage sufficient)
- Non-functional: Each LLM call must produce ≥2 verified facts or flag diminishing returns

## Architecture

```
hunger-loop-orchestrator.py
  ├── domain_prioritizer.py        ← ranks domains by user query frequency
  │     └── reads: memory.jsonl    ← counts queries per domain
  ├── gap_detector.py              ← EXISTING (LFI P2)
  │     └── reads: decision_vectors.db, domain_coverage table
  ├── question-generator.py        ← NEW: surgical research questions
  │     └── reads: existing KB facts for context
  ├── llm-researcher.py            ← NEW: fires Claude with structured output
  │     └── uses: WebSearch, WebFetch via Claude session
  ├── claim-verifier.py            ← NEW: cross-check against KB
  │     └── reads/writes: decision_vectors.db
  ├── satiation-detector.py        ← NEW: stop conditions
  │     └── reads: domain_coverage, hunger_log
  └── hunger-log.py                ← NEW: audit trail
        └── writes: hunger_log table in decision_vectors.db
```

## Related Code Files

- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/hunger-loop-orchestrator.py`

- Modify: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/data/knowledge-distillation/decision-vectors.db` — add domain_coverage + hunger_log tables

## Implementation Steps

1. **Add SQLite tables** to decision-vectors.db:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS domain_coverage (
       domain TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
       query_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       dimensions_total INTEGER DEFAULT 8,
       dimensions_filled INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       avg_confidence REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
       last_fed TEXT,
       last_gap_check TEXT
   );
   
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hunger_log (
       id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
       cycle_date TEXT NOT NULL,
       domain TEXT NOT NULL,
       facts_added INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       facts_updated INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       contradictions_found INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       coverage_before REAL,
       coverage_after REAL,
       calls_made INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       stop_reason TEXT
   );
   ```

2. **Build domain-prioritizer.py**:
   - Parse memory.jsonl → count topics per domain
   - Compute hunger_score = query_frequency × (1 - coverage) × staleness_factor
   - Return sorted list of (domain, dimension, hunger_score)
   - Handle cold start: if no query history, use equal priority

3. **Build question-generator.py**:
   - Input: (domain, dimension, existing_facts[])
   - Output: structured research question with required_output schema
   - Include anti-confirmation: "Also search [opposite query]"
   - Include existing KB context: "We already know X. Find: what we DON'T know."
   - Max 3 questions per dimension to avoid redundancy

4. **Build claim-verifier.py**:
   - Input: parsed claims from LLM response
   - Cross-check: duplicate detection (fuzzy match, threshold 0.85)
   - Cross-check: contradiction detection against existing facts
   - Cross-check: magnitude check (claim exceeds 3σ from dimension mean → FLAG)
   - Cross-check: source freshness (>180 days → tentative)
   - Output: verified_claims[], contradictions[], duplicates_merged[]

5. **Build satiation-detector.py**:
   - STOP conditions (ALL must be true):
     - Domain coverage ≥ 90% for target domain
     - No new unique facts in last 3 consecutive cycles
     - All contradictions status = RESOLVED
     - Confidence ≥ 0.8 across dimension
   - SLOW_DOWN: new_fact_rate < 1 per 5 calls → increase gap between cycles
   - WAKE_UP triggers: new /stage0 verdict, domain staleness >90 days, user query in weak domain

6. **Build hunger-loop-orchestrator.py**:
   ```python
   def run_hunger_cycle(max_calls=None):
       domains = domain_prioritizer.rank()
       for domain, dimension, score in domains:
           if satiation_detector.is_satiated(domain, dimension):
               continue
           
           questions = question_generator.create(domain, dimension)
           for q in questions:
               response = llm_researcher.research(q)  # Claude session
               claims = claim_parser.parse(response)
               verified = claim_verifier.verify(claims)
               kb.store(verified)
               hunger_log.log(domain, verified)
               
               if satiation_detector.diminishing_returns():
                   break
           
           if satiation_detector.all_satiated():
               return "SATIATED"
       
       return "CYCLE_COMPLETE"
   ```

7. **Build hunger-log.py**: Write audit trail per cycle (facts added, coverage delta, stop reason)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Orchestrator runs complete cycle: gap→question→research→verify→store
- [ ] Domain prioritizer correctly ranks by user query frequency
- [ ] Question generator produces surgical, non-generic questions with anti-confirmation
- [ ] Claim verifier catches duplicates, contradictions, magnitude outliers
- [ ] Satiation detector stops loop when coverage ≥90%
- [ ] Hunger log captures full audit trail per cycle
- [ ] Unit tests: ≥20 tests (orchestrator, prioritizer, generator, verifier, satiation)

## Risk Assessment

- **Risk**: LLM returns generic/unhelpful answers → Mitigation: question quality scoring, skip questions that yield <2 facts
- **Risk**: Infinite loop if satiation never triggers → Mitigation: hard cap at 50 calls/cycle, mandatory cooldown
- **Risk**: Domain coverage metric games itself (stores low-quality facts to fill coverage) → Mitigation: confidence-weighted coverage, not just count

# Phase 2: Hunger Loop Orchestrator

## Overview

The core loop: detect gaps → generate questions → fire LLM research → verify answers → store in KB → check satiation → repeat. Integrates with existing gap_detector.py and distillation_bridge.py from LFI.

## Requirements

- Functional: Autonomous loop that fills knowledge gaps using LLM as research tool
- Functional: User-driven domain priority (most-queried domains fed first)
- Functional: Satiation detection (stop when coverage sufficient)
- Non-functional: Each LLM call must produce ≥2 verified facts or flag diminishing returns

## Architecture

```
hunger-loop-orchestrator.py
  ├── domain_prioritizer.py        ← ranks domains by user query frequency
  │     └── reads: memory.jsonl    ← counts queries per domain
  ├── gap_detector.py              ← EXISTING (LFI P2)
  │     └── reads: decision_vectors.db, domain_coverage table
  ├── question-generator.py        ← NEW: surgical research questions
  │     └── reads: existing KB facts for context
  ├── llm-researcher.py            ← NEW: fires Claude with structured output
  │     └── uses: WebSearch, WebFetch via Claude session
  ├── claim-verifier.py            ← NEW: cross-check against KB
  │     └── reads/writes: decision_vectors.db
  ├── satiation-detector.py        ← NEW: stop conditions
  │     └── reads: domain_coverage, hunger_log
  └── hunger-log.py                ← NEW: audit trail
        └── writes: hunger_log table in decision_vectors.db
```

## Related Code Files

- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/hunger-loop-orchestrator.py`
- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/domain-prioritizer.py`
- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/question-generator.py`
- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/claim-verifier.py`
- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/satiation-detector.py`
- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/hunger-log.py`
- Modify: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/data/knowledge-distillation/decision-vectors.db` — add domain_coverage + hunger_log tables

## Implementation Steps

1. **Add SQLite tables** to decision-vectors.db:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS domain_coverage (
       domain TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
       query_count INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       dimensions_total INTEGER DEFAULT 8,
       dimensions_filled INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       avg_confidence REAL DEFAULT 0.0,
       last_fed TEXT,
       last_gap_check TEXT
   );
   
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hunger_log (
       id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
       cycle_date TEXT NOT NULL,
       domain TEXT NOT NULL,
       facts_added INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       facts_updated INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       contradictions_found INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       coverage_before REAL,
       coverage_after REAL,
       calls_made INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
       stop_reason TEXT
   );
   ```

2. **Build domain-prioritizer.py**:
   - Parse memory.jsonl → count topics per domain
   - Compute hunger_score = query_frequency × (1 - coverage) × staleness_factor
   - Return sorted list of (domain, dimension, hunger_score)
   - Handle cold start: if no query history, use equal priority

3. **Build question-generator.py**:
   - Input: (domain, dimension, existing_facts[])
   - Output: structured research question with required_output schema
   - Include anti-confirmation: "Also search [opposite query]"
   - Include existing KB context: "We already know X. Find: what we DON'T know."
   - Max 3 questions per dimension to avoid redundancy

4. **Build claim-verifier.py**:
   - Input: parsed claims from LLM response
   - Cross-check: duplicate detection (fuzzy match, threshold 0.85)
   - Cross-check: contradiction detection against existing facts
   - Cross-check: magnitude check (claim exceeds 3σ from dimension mean → FLAG)
   - Cross-check: source freshness (>180 days → tentative)
   - Output: verified_claims[], contradictions[], duplicates_merged[]

5. **Build satiation-detector.py**:
   - STOP conditions (ALL must be true):
     - Domain coverage ≥ 90% for target domain
     - No new unique facts in last 3 consecutive cycles
     - All contradictions status = RESOLVED
     - Confidence ≥ 0.8 across dimension
   - SLOW_DOWN: new_fact_rate < 1 per 5 calls → increase gap between cycles
   - WAKE_UP triggers: new /stage0 verdict, domain staleness >90 days, user query in weak domain

6. **Build hunger-loop-orchestrator.py**:
   ```python
   def run_hunger_cycle(max_calls=None):
       domains = domain_prioritizer.rank()
       for domain, dimension, score in domains:
           if satiation_detector.is_satiated(domain, dimension):
               continue
           
           questions = question_generator.create(domain, dimension)
           for q in questions:
               response = llm_researcher.research(q)  # Claude session
               claims = claim_parser.parse(response)
               verified = claim_verifier.verify(claims)
               kb.store(verified)
               hunger_log.log(domain, verified)
               
               if satiation_detector.diminishing_returns():
                   break
           
           if satiation_detector.all_satiated():
               return "SATIATED"
       
       return "CYCLE_COMPLETE"
   ```

7. **Build hunger-log.py**: Write audit trail per cycle (facts added, coverage delta, stop reason)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Orchestrator runs complete cycle: gap→question→research→verify→store
- [ ] Domain prioritizer correctly ranks by user query frequency
- [ ] Question generator produces surgical, non-generic questions with anti-confirmation
- [ ] Claim verifier catches duplicates, contradictions, magnitude outliers
- [ ] Satiation detector stops loop when coverage ≥90%
- [ ] Hunger log captures full audit trail per cycle
- [ ] Unit tests: ≥20 tests (orchestrator, prioritizer, generator, verifier, satiation)

## Risk Assessment

- **Risk**: LLM returns generic/unhelpful answers → Mitigation: question quality scoring, skip questions that yield <2 facts
- **Risk**: Infinite loop if satiation never triggers → Mitigation: hard cap at 50 calls/cycle, mandatory cooldown
- **Risk**: Domain coverage metric games itself (stores low-quality facts to fill coverage) → Mitigation: confidence-weighted coverage, not just count

# Phase 3: Post-Verdict Auto-Distill

## Overview

Extract structured claims from every /stage0 run's Wave 1/2 agent outputs. This is FREE intelligence — already paid for by the /stage0 LLM calls. Currently these insights die in verdict markdown. This phase captures them permanently.

## Requirements

- Functional: After every /stage0 verdict, extract all agent claims into decision_vectors.db
- Functional: Track which /stage0 case generated each fact (provenance)
- Functional: Queue newly discovered gaps for next hunger cycle
- Non-functional: Add <5 seconds to post-verdict processing

## Architecture

```
/stage0 verdict generated (Step 7)
  → Step 9: persist-verdict.py (existing)
  → Step 9.1: post-verdict-distiller.py (NEW)
      ├── Parse all Wave 1 agent outputs (8 agents)
      ├── Parse all Wave 2 agent outputs (6 agents)
      ├── claim-parser.py (from P1) extracts claims
      ├── claim-verifier.py (from P2) validates
      ├── Store verified claims in decision_vectors.db
      ├── Update domain_coverage scores
      └── Queue gaps discovered → hunger_queue table
```

## Related Code Files

- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/post-verdict-distiller.py`
- Modify: Stage0 spec — add Step 9.1 after Step 9 (persist verdict)
- Modify: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/data/knowledge-distillation/decision-vectors.db` — add hunger_queue table

## Implementation Steps

1. **Add hunger_queue table**:
   ```sql
   CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS hunger_queue (
       id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
       domain TEXT NOT NULL,
       dimension TEXT NOT NULL,
       gap_description TEXT NOT NULL,
       source_case_id TEXT,
       priority REAL DEFAULT 0.5,
       status TEXT DEFAULT 'PENDING',
       created_at TEXT DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
   );
   ```

2. **Build post-verdict-distiller.py**:
   - Input: case JSON from /tmp/case-{case_id}.json (contains all agent outputs)
   - For each agent output in case JSON:
     - If JSON format → claim_parser.parse() directly
     - If prose → agent_output_adapter.extract_claims_from_prose()
   - Run claim_verifier.verify() on all extracted claims
   - Store verified claims with `query_origin = case_id`
   - Update domain_coverage table
   - Scan for gaps: dimensions with <3 facts or confidence <0.5 → queue

3. **Wire into stage0 pipeline**:
   - After Step 9 (persist-verdict.py) succeeds
   - Call: `post-verdict-distiller.distill(case_json_path)`
   - Non-blocking: if distiller fails, log warning but don't block verdict display
   - Report: "Distilled X claims, updated Y domain scores, queued Z gaps"

4. **Gap queue prioritization**:
   - Priority = (1 - current_dimension_coverage) × domain_query_frequency
   - Hunger loop (P2) reads from hunger_queue before gap_detector
   - Dedup: don't queue same gap twice

## Success Criteria

- [ ] Distiller extracts ≥5 claims per typical /stage0 verdict
- [ ] Claims stored with correct case_id provenance
- [ ] Domain coverage scores update after each distillation
- [ ] Gaps queued for next hunger cycle with correct priority
- [ ] Processing time <5 seconds per verdict
- [ ] Non-blocking: distiller failure doesn't block Step 10 (display)
- [ ] Unit tests: ≥10 tests (parsing, storage, gap queuing, coverage update)

## Risk Assessment

- **Risk**: Agent outputs too varied to parse reliably → Mitigation: prose adapter handles fallback, accuracy improves as P1 schema adoption grows
- **Risk**: Too many low-quality claims stored → Mitigation: confidence floor 0.3, claims below rejected
- **Risk**: Gap queue grows unbounded → Mitigation: max 50 pending gaps per domain, oldest auto-expire after 30 days

# Phase 4: Feed Command and Hook Wiring

## Overview

Wire the hunger loop into 3 trigger points: (1) /feed command for manual trigger, (2) SessionStart hook for automatic feeding, (3) post-verdict hook for auto-distill. Makes the system actively hungry every time user opens Claude Code.

## Requirements

- Functional: /feed command triggers manual hunger cycle with progress output
- Functional: SessionStart hook runs micro hunger cycle (top 3 domains, cap 10 calls)
- Functional: Post-verdict hook triggers distiller automatically
- Non-functional: SessionStart adds <30 seconds to session load

## Architecture

```
User opens Claude Code
  → SessionStart hook fires
  → hunger-session-start.cjs

# Phase 5: Satiation Calibration and Testing

## Overview

Calibrate stop conditions, test convergence behavior, verify the system actually gets smarter over time. Ensure it doesn't loop forever or stop too early. Integration test across all components.

## Requirements

- Functional: Satiation thresholds tuned from real /stage0 runs
- Functional: Convergence test — KB quality improves measurably over 5+ cycles
- Functional: Dashboard showing domain health, coverage trends, hunger history
- Non-functional: System reaches 90% coverage in top 3 domains within 20 hunger cycles

## Architecture

```
Calibration workflow:
  1. Seed: Run 5 /stage0 verdicts across different domains
  2. Measure: Check decision_vectors.db growth, domain coverage
  3. Feed: Run 3 full hunger cycles
  4. Measure: Coverage delta, fact quality, satiation triggers
  5. Tune: Adjust thresholds if convergence too slow/fast
  6. Verify: Run 2 more /stage0 verdicts, check local pre-screen improvement
```

## Related Code Files

- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/test-hunger-integration.py`
- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/hunger-dashboard.py` — CLI dashboard
- Create: `D:/code/invesments/master_investments/.claude/lib/intelligence/hunger/calibration-config.json`
- Modify: satiation-detector.py — apply calibrated thresholds

## Implementation Steps

1. **Create calibration-config.json**:
   ```json
   {
     "satiation": {
       "coverage_threshold": 0.90,
       "confidence_threshold": 0.80,
       "no_new_facts_cycles": 3,
       "diminishing_returns_ratio": 0.2,
       "max_calls_per_cycle": 50,
       "micro_mode_max_calls": 10,
       "session_start_cooldown_hours": 6,
       "gap_queue_max_per_domain": 50,
       "gap_expiry_days": 30,
       "dedup_similarity_threshold": 0.85,
       "confidence_floor": 0.30,
       "staleness_days": 180
     },
     "dimensions": [
       "failure_rates", "unit_economics", "competitive_landscape",
       "moat_patterns", "founder_paths", "timing_windows",
       "regulatory_risks", "compounding_mechanisms"
     ],
     "domains_active": []
   }
   ```

2. **Build hunger-dashboard.py**:
   - `--summary`: one-line per domain (coverage%, confidence%, last_fed, query_count)
   - `--detail <domain>`: per-dimension breakdown with fact count, avg confidence, staleness
   - `--history`: last 10 hunger cycles with facts added, coverage delta
   - `--queue`: pending gaps sorted by priority
   - Output: formatted table for CLI display

3. **Build integration test** (test-hunger-integration.py):
   - Test 1: Cold start — empty DB, run 1 hunger cycle, verify ≥10 facts stored
   - Test 2: Convergence — run 5 cycles, verify coverage monotonically increases
   - Test 3: Satiation — seed domain to 90% coverage, verify loop stops
   - Test 4: Dedup — inject duplicate facts, verify no double-counting
   - Test 5: Contradiction — inject conflicting facts, verify flagged
   - Test 6: Post-verdict — simulate case JSON, verify distiller extracts ≥5 claims
   - Test 7: Domain priority — simulate query history, verify most-queried domain fed first
   - Test 8: Hook chain — verify SessionStart → evolution → hunger sequence
   - Test 9: /feed command — verify full cycle runs with progress output
   - Test 10: Diminishing returns — feed same domain 10 times, verify slowdown

4. **Calibration run**:
   - Run hunger cycle on 2 known domains (saas, ecommerce)
   - Measure: facts/call ratio, time per cycle, coverage curve
   - Adjust thresholds if:
     - coverage_threshold too high (never satiated) → lower to 0.85
     - confidence_threshold too strict → lower to 0.7
     - diminishing_returns_ratio too sensitive → raise to 0.3

5. **Verify local pre-screen improvement**:
   - Before: Step 1.8 has 205 vectors → limited pre-screen
   - After: 500+ vectors → test if local pre-screen catches more cases
   - Measure: % of queries where local confidence ≥0.7 (can skip full LLM pipeline)

## Success Criteria

- [ ] All 10 integration tests pass
- [ ] Convergence verified: 5 cycles → coverage increases monotonically
- [ ] Satiation triggers correctly at configured thresholds
- [ ] Dashboard shows accurate domain health metrics
- [ ] Calibration config tuned from real data (not just defaults)
- [ ] Local pre-screen improvement measurable (% queries handled locally increases)
- [ ] No infinite loops in any test scenario (hard cap enforced)
- [ ] Hook chain executes in correct order without conflicts

## Risk Assessment

- **Risk**: Real-world convergence slower than test scenarios → Mitigation: lower initial thresholds, track over 2-week period
- **Risk**: Dashboard adds maintenance burden → Mitigation: read-only from SQLite, no additional state
- **Risk**: Calibration overfits to test domains → Mitigation: test with ≥3 diverse domains (saas, physical, content)
